q: Do Verra and Gold Standard accept digital MRV data?
title: Do registries accept digital MRV?
short: Yes, as monitoring data, but not in place of verification. Verra and Gold Standard accept data gathered by meters, sensors, satellites or software if it meets the monitoring rules of the approved methodology and an accredited validation and verification body checks it. Credits are issued only after that verification.
audience: Developers and MSMEs considering dMRV tools

sections.h: What decides whether digital data is accepted
ul: The methodology. Each approved methodology lists the parameters to monitor, how often, and the equipment and calibration required. Digital data must match those parameters.
The monitoring plan in the registered project description, which names the data source and procedures.
The verifier. An accredited validation and verification body (VVB) must be able to trace each figure back to its source and test the data system.
p: A digital tool can make that trail faster to check. It does not change what the methodology asks for.

Both Verra and Gold Standard have run consultations and pilots on digital MRV, covering automated data collection, remote sensing and digital submission of monitoring reports. These aim to make review easier; neither has dropped third-party verification.

The Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market's Core Carbon Principles also require robust quantification and independent validation and verification, so a programme cannot accept unverified data and keep CCP approval.

sections.h: What a VVB will look for in digital data
ol: Meter or sensor make, serial number and calibration certificates.
Raw data kept unchanged, with a record of any cleaning, gap filling or estimates.
Access controls and an audit log showing who changed what.
A way to tie each total back to raw readings or source documents, such as invoices.
Back-up data or a conservative default for periods when the device failed.

p: Some platforms describe themselves as registry-approved or promise faster issuance. Ask which methodology the data serves, whether a VVB has accepted it in a real verification, and get that in writing. Registration and issuance timelines still depend on the registry and the verifier.

senseible: Senseible keeps a digital evidence trail: each uploaded invoice, bill or fuel slip carries a SHA-256 fingerprint, and the figure read from it can be traced back to the file. It does not submit anything to Verra or Gold Standard, is not a VVB, and makes no claim about verification cost or time.
